note: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/Simulating Urban Patterns of Life- A Geo-Social Data Generation Framework.md

primary_source.version: Kim et al., SIGSPATIAL 2019, four-page conference paper; NSF Public Access Repository copy.
primary_source.coverage: Read full four-page source sequentially: title/authors/venue/abstract; §1 motivation and requirements; §2 trigger/behavior/action/goal semantics, competing priority, library/builder/encoder/simulator/decoder; §3 demonstration, model fields and HUNGRY example, MASON/GeoMASON setup, visual results, streaming and Spark/Zeppelin; §4 conclusion/future work; all five figure captions and the full 26-entry bibliography.

claim_checks.claim: Abstract describes privacy/cost/quality motivations, richer agent behaviors in realistic geo-social worlds, configurable drag-and-drop modeling, scalable trajectory generation and real-time API streaming.
claim_checks.result: PASS; note abstract faithfully matches the primary abstract.

claim_checks.claim: Trigger responds to internal/external changes; behavior is initiated by trigger and contains actions; action has one or more steps and produces output upon goal completion; outputs may feed subsequent actions.
claim_checks.result: PASS; matches the paper definitions and Fig. 1.

claim_checks.claim: Competing behavior priority is modeler-defined; Maslow is an example hypothesis, not a universal algorithm or numerical scale.
claim_checks.result: PASS; appropriately avoids inventing a priority rule.

claim_checks.claim: Architecture comprises shared component library, drag-and-drop Model Builder/Encoder and Simulator/Decoder; generated check-ins, transactions and meetings can go to file or stream; builder implementation uses Java/JGraphX.

Demonstration model includes food/sleep triggers; eight listed properties and eating/sleeping/working/doNothing behaviors; food need threshold >50; restaurant choice, shortest-path travel, eating until the full goal, then bill payment.
claim_checks.result: PASS; note scopes these mechanics to the demonstration model. The 100% food-level interpretation is consistent with the source’s general goal example and untilFULL action goal, but the source does not provide a richer universal goal semantics.

claim_checks.claim: Demonstration runs MASON/GeoMASON with 10,000 agents over synthetic spatial data of 14,181 road segments; daily routine screenshots are visual output and do not establish empirical validation.
claim_checks.result: PASS; note preserves authors’ distinction between visual display and possible trace validation.
claim_checks.source_location: §3 Simulation and Data Generation; Fig. 3; trace-validation paragraph.

claim_checks.claim: Streaming includes agent ID, simulation timestamp/tick, current location and status; ZeroMQ is used; Zeppelin/Spark Streaming is the illustrated consumer.
Applicability is framework-level and modeler-configured; conclusion treats a plausible general pattern-of-life model and further scalability work as future work.
claim_checks.result: PASS; note does not overstate the stylized demonstration as an empirically validated general behavior model.
